issue: Setting matches: x successes in n independent draws with one unknown p, central interval with 2.5 % in each tail. The repo's clopper_pearson (tools/_ch5_style.py) is the beta-quantile form of these limits; the paper itself reads them off interpolated charts, but the name is the field's convention for the exact limits. claim: Clopper-Pearson applies to every ASP the dissertation reports, including the APT attacker model's ASP averaged over c1 to c4.
quote:
A sample of n units is randomly drawn from a very large population in which
the proportion of units bearing a certain character, A, is p.
issue: The limits are for one population with one p. An ASP averaged over four attack profiles, each with its own p, is not that setting: the pooled count is not binomial (it is a sum of binomials with different p), so the interval's 95 % coverage is not what the paper establishes. tools/ch5_sweep_figures.py:506 also rebuilds the count as round(asp * n) from an averaged ASP; whether n there is per-profile or pooled should be checked. Minor if the averaged ASP's interval is not printed; otherwise say what it is.
fix_text: Clopper--Pearson for the ASP of one attacker or attack profile \citep{clopper1934use}
